summary: The Motor Vehicle Modernization Act of 2026 directs the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to update and modernize its motor vehicle safety programs, research plans, and consumer information tools. It establishes new offices, advisory committees, and working groups to focus on automated driving systems, vehicle safety ratings, recalls, and post-crash rescue, while also adjusting exemption limits and review requirements for existing safety standards.

affected_groups.effect: Must navigate updated NHTSA priority plans, participate in voluntary NCAP performance testing, benefit from higher general exemption vehicle caps (up to 90,000 vehicles), and comply with modernized recall notification and safety defect timelines.
Tasked with creating new offices, priority plans, review cycles, advisory committees, working groups, and conducting multiple specialized studies and reports for Congress.

Impacted by expanded consumer education campaigns on vehicle automation and safety ratings, modernized electronic recall notifications, and potential future changes to vehicle safety ratings and standards.
Involved through a dedicated Motor Vehicle Fire Rescue Working Group to evaluate post-crash extraction, battery fire suppression, and rescue tools.

key_provisions: Requires the NHTSA Administrator to develop and publish a comprehensive 36-month motor vehicle safety rulemaking and research priority plan every two years.
Establishes an Office of the New Car Assessment Program (NCAP) led by an Associate Administrator and creates a voluntary performance testing program for manufacturers.
Establishes an NCAP Advisory Committee of 18 members to evaluate safety technologies and report on the feasibility of a public-private partnership or nonprofit entity to run the NCAP.
Mandates that the Administrator review existing motor vehicle safety standards every four years to determine if they should be revised or eliminated.
Increases the vehicle threshold for general safety exemptions from 2,500 vehicles to 90,000 vehicles and sets a 1-year decision deadline for exemption applications.
Creates working groups focused on consumer education regarding vehicle automation and post-crash motor vehicle fire rescue operations.
Requires studies on passenger motor vehicle ownership costs, automated wheelchair securement systems, modernization of Vehicle Identification Numbers (VINs), and recall completion rates.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or appropriations required to carry out the new offices, working groups, and studies.
Detailed criteria for how the Secretary will evaluate specific equivalent safety levels under the expanded general exemptions.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Motor Vehicle Modernization Act of 2026 directs the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to update and modernize its motor vehicle safety programs, research plans, and consumer information tools. It establishes new offices, advisory committees, and working groups to focus on automated driving systems, vehicle safety ratings, recalls, and post-crash rescue, while also adjusting exemption limits and review requirements for existing safety standards.
summary_detail.significance: The bill broadly alters federal motor vehicle safety administration by institutionalizing regular planning, reforming consumer testing programs, expanding exemption parameters for smaller manufacturers or new technologies, and mandating extensive studies on modern automotive trends like automation, electrification, and vehicle ownership costs.
